title: Slide open a small stiff window by its delicate handle
instruction: The window is stiff and its handle is delicate. Grip the handle and slide the window open.
context: Robots in homes, care homes and offices will open windows, cabinet doors and hatches whose runners have stiffened, by handles that are often small plastic or glued-on fittings. A stiff sash sticks until it is pulled hard enough to break free, then slides more easily; pulling harder than the handle can bear, or yanking on after the sash has reached its stop, tears the handle off.
setup: Station table with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. All sizes and positions in cm, positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the table top. Window: a small white sliding window fixed to the table, its frame and sash white uPVC (PVC-U) profile and its panes 3 mm float glass, its frame 2.8 deep (x 28.6 to 31.4), 52.4 wide (y 21.2 to -31.2) and 20.4 tall, with a 1.2 sill, head and jambs around an opening 18 tall from y 20 to -30. Right half: a fixed glazed pane (3 mm glass in a frame 1.4 wide) at the back of the frame. Left half: the sash, a glazed frame 23 wide (y 20 to -3), 18 tall and 1.2 deep at the front of the frame (x 28.7 to 29.9), 500 g, that slides right in front of the fixed pane, up to 24. It slides on the frame's uPVC track and is closed at the start. It is stiff: it stays put until pulled along the track with 10 N, then slides with a steady 7 N drag at any speed (dry friction), and stops at 24 cm open. For real trials this comes from M6 spring plungers (catalogue parts, for example TE-CO 69704X: 6 N initial, 17 N final end force), two or three screwed up through a hardwood block fixed under the sill so their noses press on the sash's bottom rail, screwed in or out until a spring scale on the handle reads 10 N when the closed sash starts to move and 7 N while it slides at about 2 cm/s. Handle: a chrome-plated zinc D-handle on the sash's right edge, at y -2.3: a grip bar 1 (x) x 1.2 (y) x 7 tall, 5.7 to 12.7 above the table, held 3.2 out from the sash's face (x 24.5 to 25.5) by two stand-offs. It tears off if pulled with more than about 14 N: for real trials each stand-off is held to a steel washer screwed to the sash by a 16 mm countersunk neodymium pot magnet (Supermagnete CSN-16, displacement force about 7.85 N each, so about 15.7 N for the pair). Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Only opening pulled by the handle alone counts, kept as a running total: add the sash's opening while a gripper is closed on the handle's grip bar pulling it and no other part of the robot touches the sash, its glass or the frame; subtract any closing, however it happens. Pushing the sash, pushing the handle without gripping it, a light pull on the handle while something else pushes, or the sash moving after the gripper lets go adds nothing, and pulling a little, closing and pulling again earns no more than the last pull. The total is never more than how far the sash is open. In real trials, from the video and a ruler: mark the sash's position whenever a gripper closes on or lets go of the grip bar, whenever another robot part touches the sash, glass or frame or stops touching it, and whenever the sash starts closing or stops; add the openings made in the counting stretches and subtract every closing. In the simulation: opening counts while a gripper's tool point is within 1 cm of the grip bar's centre, its fingers are closed on the bar, the handle's fixings have given at least 1 mm (0.8 N), no link of either arm touches the frame, the sash or its glass, and none touches the handle except the gripping hand (PhysX contact forces over 0.01 N between every robot link and the window), and the sash's force balance shows no other force helping it open by more than 2 N. With the handle on, by the total at the end: 1.0 at 15 cm or more (in the simulation the trial ends with 1.0 once the sash has moved under 1 cm/s for 1 s), 0.75 at 12 to 15 cm, 0.5 at 8 to 12 cm, 0.25 at 4 to 8 cm, 0 under 4 cm. Score 0 if the handle has torn off or come loose at any point (in the simulation: it gave 1.8 cm along the sash, which takes about 14 N), or if the glass or frame is damaged. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the sash closed after each trial. Before each session, check the friction pad with a spring scale on the handle: about 10 N to start the closed sash moving and 7 N while it slides; turn the set screw to adjust. Check the handle's magnets with the spring scale pulling along the sash: it should let go at about 14 N (13 to 16 N; a thin plastic shim under each magnet lowers the force). After a tear, set the handle back on its washers.
fidelity: Approximate. The window is rigid boxes. The sash's stiffness is dry friction: it holds until pulled with 10 N, then drags with 7 N at any speed, matching the friction pad. The handle's fixings are a spring that gives up to 1.8 cm before tearing at about 14 N; a real handle gives far less. Nothing else can bend or break, so the glass and frame rule applies only to real trials. Robot contact with the window is read from PhysX contact forces on every arm link.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm, right of the video, reached the handle by 8 s and prodded it until about 50 s but never gripped it; the sash moved 0.7 mm; the left arm, left of the video, stayed by the window's left end); demo: 1.0
